spec.title: k6 VUs (now)
spec.description: From k6 remote-write. Adjust if your k6 metric name differs.

spec.title: Open FDs vs limit
spec.description: MAIN PANEL. The open-fds line should flatten against the dashed limit line.

spec.title: Connections vs fds vs handles
spec.description: Connections should track fds with a constant offset. VUs show the offered concurrency; the gap after saturation is rejected connections.

spec.title: Accepted connections / s
spec.description: Should stop growing at the limit even though VUs keep rising.

spec.title: Server errors / s by code
spec.description: EMFILE appears here if Node surfaces it through server.on('error'). Empty means libuv dropped silently.

spec.title: Total connections accepted (cumulative)
spec.description: Flat line = no new connection was accepted.

spec.title: FD utilization
spec.description: open fds / RLIMIT_NOFILE for the Node process. Red = close to EMFILE.

spec.title: k6 VUs and request rate
spec.description: Requests/s with /io?ms=5000 stays low by design; VUs are what matter.

spec.title: k6 failed request ratio
spec.description: Rate metric exported by k6 remote write. It is cumulative over the run, so look for where it starts rising, not its absolute value.

spec.title: Event loop lag
spec.description: Should stay flat: the loop is idle, the limit is the fd table.

spec.title: Process CPU (cores)
spec.description: 1.0 = one full core. Should stay low.

spec.title: Scrape health (up)
spec.description: Drops to 0 or gaps if /metrics could not be served while saturated.

spec.title: Open FDs
spec.description: process_open_fds

spec.title: System fd table usage
spec.description: Should stay near zero. Proves this is RLIMIT_NOFILE (per process), not fs.file-max.

spec.title: Listen queue (if exporter script provides it)
spec.description: From your listen-queue-exporter textfile script. Metric name may differ; edit or delete.

spec.title: Server CPUs busy (per logical CPU)
spec.description: CPUs in the $server_cpus regex (top bar). Workers should spread over the pinned cores; SMT siblings share one physical core.

spec.title: Generator (k6) CPUs: headroom check
spec.description: CPUs in $gen_cpus. Keep below 70% (red line) or the result is not trustworthy.

spec.title: Latency percentiles (k6 native histogram, log axis)
spec.description: True per-window percentiles via histogram_quantile(rate()). Dashed line = 50 ms. Needs k6 TREND_AS_NATIVE_HISTOGRAM=true and Prometheus --enable-feature=native-histograms.

spec.title: FD limit
spec.description: process_max_fds (ulimit -n of the server process)

spec.title: Open connections
spec.description: Custom gauge: sockets currently open on the server

spec.title: Peak open FDs (range)
spec.description: Highest fd count in the selected time range. Compare with the limit.

spec.title: Server errors (range)
spec.description: Server-level errors (accept EMFILE etc.) during the range

spec.title: Scrape health
spec.description: 0 = Prometheus could not scrape /metrics (can happen at fd saturation)

spec.title: Baseline FDs (not connections)
spec.description: open fds minus open connections: stdio, epoll, listener, libs. This is the headroom you lose before any client connects.

spec.expr: max(process_open_fds{job="eventpulse-nodejs", instance=~"$instance"} - on(instance, job) sum by (instance, job) (http_connections_open{job="eventpulse-nodejs", instance=~"$instance"}))

spec.title: E0.5 summary: is the process at its fd ceiling?
Core evidence: fds, connections and the ceiling
System-wide context (node_exporter): the system table is not full, the per-process limit is
